studies.title: Executive dysfunction in Parkinson's disease is associated with altered pallidal-frontal processing.
studies.abstract: Executive dysfunction in Parkinson's disease is well documented, but it is still unclear whether this results from (i) prefrontal dysfunction, (ii) striatal dysfunction, or (iii) altered striatal outflow to the prefrontal cortex. To clarify this issue, we used H(2)(15)O PET to asses six nondemented and nondepressed patients with Parkinson's disease and six matched controls while they performed a task involving executive function, random number generation (RNG), and a control counting task. To assess the effect of increasing task demands, each task was performed at three rates. Both groups showed significant increase in nonrandomness of responses during RNG at faster rates, which was differentially greater for the patients at the faster rate. The controls showed significant activation of the lateral and medial prefrontal cortex and superior and medial parietal cortex during RNG relative to counting. For the same comparison, the patients did not show any activity in medial frontal structures. The controls showed significantly greater mesial frontotemporal activation during counting than RNG, whereas the patients did not show any modulation of regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) in these areas with task. With faster rates of RNG, the controls showed rCBF increase in the right internal segment of globus pallidus (GPi) and a decrease in frontal cortex. The patients showed the opposite pattern of subcortical and frontal rCBF change with faster rates. The results suggest that executive dysfunction in Parkinson's disease is associated with a failure to modulate frontal activation with increased task demands (nature of task or rate), a deficit associated with altered rCBF in the GPi, the final basal ganglia output pathway to frontal cortex rather than any intrinsic prefrontal dysfunction.

studies.title: Prefrontal mechanisms for executive control over emotional distraction are altered in major depression.
studies.abstract: A dysfunction in the interaction between executive function and mood regulation has been proposed as the pathophysiology of depression. However, few studies have investigated the alteration in brain systems related to executive control over emotional distraction in depression. To address this issue, 19 patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) and 20 healthy controls were scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging. Participants performed an emotional oddball task in which infrequently presented circle targets required detection while sad and neutral pictures were irrelevant novel distractors. Hemodynamic responses were compared for targets, sad distractors, and for targets that followed sad or neutral distractors (Target-after-Sad and Target-after-Neutral). Patients with MDD revealed attenuated activation overall to targets in executive brain regions. Behaviorally, MDD patients were slower in response to Target-after-Sad than Target-after-Neutra stimuli. Patients also revealed a reversed activation pattern from controls in response to this contrast in the left anterior cingulate, insula, right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), and bilateral middle frontal gyrus. Those patients who engaged the right IFG more during Target-after-Neutral stimuli responded faster to targets, confirming a role of this region in coping with emotional distraction. The results provide direct evidence of an alteration in the neural systems that interplay cognition with mood in MDD.

studies.title: Disturbances in selective information processing associated with the BDNF Val66Met polymorphism: evidence from cognition, the P300 and fronto-hippocampal systems.
studies.abstract: In this study, we examined whether the Met allele of the BDNF Val66Met polymorphism is associated with selective disruptions to task-relevant information processing. In 475 non-clinical participants for whom BDNF genotype status was determined we used the 'IntegNeuro' computerized battery of neuropsychological tests to assess cognitive performance, an auditory oddball task to elicit the P300 event-related potential (ERP) and, in smaller subsets of these subjects, high resolution structural MRI imaging to quantify fronto-hippocampal grey matter (n=161), and functional magnetic resonance imaging to assess fronto-hippocampal BOLD activation (n=37). Met/Met (MM) homozygotes had higher verbal recall errors, in the absence of differences in attention, executive function, verbal ability or sensori-motor function. Further, MM homozygotes demonstrated a slowed P300 ERP during the oddball task, with corresponding alterations in hippocampal and lateral prefrontal activation, and a localized reduction in hippocampal grey matter. These results are consistent with a subtle impact of the Met allele on fronto-hippocampal systems involved in selective information processing of stimulus context and memory updating within the normal population. The findings also indicate that heritable endophenotypes such as the P300 have value in elucidating genotype-phenotype relationships.

studies.title: Neural correlates of decision making with explicit information about probabilities and incentives in elderly healthy subjects.
studies.abstract: Recent functional neuroimaging and lesion studies demonstrate the involvement of the orbitofrontal/ventromedial prefrontal cortex as a key structure in decision making processes. This region seems to be particularly crucial when contingencies between options and consequences are unknown but have to be learned by the use of feedback following previous decisions (decision making under ambiguity). However, little is known about the neural correlates of decision making under risk conditions in which information about probabilities and potential outcomes is given. In the present study, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging to measure blood-oxygenation-level-dependent (BOLD) responses in 12 subjects during a decision making task. This task provided explicit information about probabilities and associated potential incentives. The responses were compared to BOLD signals in a control condition without information about incentives. In contrast to previous decision making studies, we completely removed the outcome phase following a decision to exclude the potential influence of feedback previously received on current decisions. The results indicate that the integration of information about probabilities and incentives leads to activations within the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, the posterior parietal lobe, the anterior cingulate and the right lingual gyrus. We assume that this pattern of activation is due to the involvement of executive functions, conflict detection mechanisms and arithmetic operations during the deliberation phase of decisional processes that are based on explicit information.

studies.fulltext_screening_reason: This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (overt verbal fluency) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and within-group contrasts. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, with voxelwise statistics (SPM5) and FDR correction across the brain and coordinates/figures reported. Participant groups include healthy controls and schizophrenia patients. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). This is a PET task-based study of dual-task/divided attention (central executive) in amnestic MCI, reporting within-group task>rest contrasts and group comparisons. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based PET of executive function), I6 (task falls within executive domains - divided attention/working memory), I8 (reports within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant group allowed), and I10 (results reported with peak locations/coordinates). However, the group-level analyses were conducted after masking contrast images with an a priori prefrontal ROI (BAs 44/45/46); no whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps were reported. Thus it fails I7 and meets exclusion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study probing cognitive flexibility using a verbal Trail Making Test (vTMT), an executive function (set-shifting) task. The paper reports whole-brain BOLD acquisition and intersubject voxelwise GLM analyses with corrected thresholds and cluster criteria, and presents group-level within-subject contrasts (vTMTB > vTMTA) with activation tables and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that examines attention shifting (cross-modal focus vs shift), a form of cognitive flexibility and inhibitory control relevant to executive function. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (ANOVA, voxelwise Z maps, cluster correction) and presents within-group task contrasts (Focus-Auditory, Focus-Visual, Shift vs baseline and comparisons). Results are reported across figures and tables with Talairach coordinates. Participant groups (healthy younger and older adults) are acceptable per criteria. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study used a task-based executive function paradigm (MCST) and reports within-group contrasts, but the voxelwise statistical analysis and inference were confined to the striatum (search volume and correction assumed the entire striatum and authors state only peaks within the striatum were considered). Thus the study does not provide a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map independent of an a priori ROI. Exclusion criterion E3 (ROI / small-volume-corrected analyses only) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based executive function), I6 (tasks assessing planning/set-shifting - established executive domains), I8 (within-group task contrast: retrieval with shift vs without shift), I9 (healthy participant group acceptable), I10 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise evidence not provided; analysis confined to a priori striatal region). Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET task-based study using 11C-raclopride during a spatial working memory (executive) task (SWT) with a visuomotor control (VMT). The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (within-group SWT vs VMT contrasts for controls and PD patients, and between-group comparisons), providing whole-brain statistical maps and tables/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria: I5 (PET task-based executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for both groups), I9 (clinical and control participant groups allowed), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using somatosensory Go/Nogo tasks that assess executive functions (response execution and inhibition). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects), with within-group contrasts (Movement Go, Count Go, Go vs Nogo comparisons) and thresholding details; results are described with anatomical coordinates/regions. Participants are healthy adults. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is original empirical neuroimaging work). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based Tower of London paradigm that probes planning (an established executive function). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise PET analyses (with thresholds and peak coordinates/tables/figures), within-group contrasts (EXPT1 vs 1-move control; regression across blocks; EXPT10 vs EXPT1) for both patients and controls, and provides coordinates and ROI follow-ups. Participant groups include clinical (Parkinson’s) and healthy controls. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory in PTSD and controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group contrasts (VT>FT and FT>FIX) analyzed with SPM2 and FDR correction, with tables/figures and coordinates described. Tasks fall within the executive function domain (working memory/updating). A within-group task contrast is reported for both participant groups. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (task switching/cognitive flexibility) with both young and older groups. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (switching vs. nonswitching contrasts) thresholded and described in the text/figures, meeting the meta-analysis requirement for task-evoked activation maps. The task falls squarely within executive function domains (cognitive control/cognitive flexibility). Multiple within-group contrasts are reported for each age group, and results are presented as whole-brain maps and ROI-derived magnitudes. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET study of working memory (executive function) with task-based paradigms (memory search and 2-back). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 (random-effects second-level t-maps) and presents within-group contrasts (memory search vs control; 2-back vs control) with thresholding and tables of results. Methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Therefore it satisfies executive-function task imaging, voxelwise whole-brain analyses, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

The study used FDG-PET acquired during 'mental rest' (resting-state metabolic scans) and did not employ a task-based fMRI/PET paradigm or report any within-group task activation contrasts. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring task-based executive-function imaging (I5, I6, I7, I8). The study does meet I9 (participant group acceptable) and I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results are reported as coordinates), but exclusion criterion E4 applies (resting-state analyses without a task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm of intrinsic alertness (vigilance), which falls within the executive-function domains specified. Methods describe group-level, voxelwise analyses using SPM (including across-subject voxelwise correlation analyses and reference voxels), and Table 1 lists representative voxel coordinates; the paper compares task conditions within-group (alertness vs fixation) and reports statistical results (path coefficients, omnibus Chi-square difference). Participants and full methods/results/discussion are present. Although the paper emphasizes connectivity (CSEM), it derives its network modules from voxelwise activation clusters and presents voxelwise correlation analyses and coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked evidence. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based PET study of visual working memory (an executive function) that reports within-group, voxelwise group analyses using SPM99 with whole-brain contrasts (e.g., SPA vs AM, NSPA vs AM, SPA vs NSPA). Results are reported as stereotaxic coordinates and tables and ROI analyses supplement voxelwise results. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for modality (PET), domain (working memory), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, and reporting format. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper is a quantitative meta-analysis of previously published fMRI studies rather than an original empirical fMRI/PET study reporting new, within-group voxelwise task activation maps. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper: meta-analysis without original human neuroimaging data) applies. The article does address executive-function domains (task switching and Stroop — I5 and I6 are satisfied) and reports coordinates/tables derived from prior whole-brain studies (I10). However, it does not present original group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (I7 not met) nor original within-group task contrasts from primary neuroimaging data (I8 not met). Therefore it must be excluded under E6.

This is a PET study using an attention (Continuous Performance) task, so it meets I5 (task-based PET) and I6 (vigilance/executive domain). Participants include clinical first-episode schizophrenia patients, satisfying I9. However, the paper reports region-based (Talairach ROI/cell) metabolic and volumetric analyses and group-level ROI statistics and correlations rather than any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or within-group voxelwise task contrasts. Therefore it fails to meet I7 (no voxelwise whole-brain task-activation map reported) and I8 (no within-group task contrast map reported). This corresponds to exclusion criteria E3 (only ROI analyses/no voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-group task activation contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study assessing spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM99 analyses (whole-brain exploratory search and small-volume corrections in frontal ROIs) and within-group task contrasts (structured and non-structured span versus visuomotor control), with corrected voxelwise thresholds and coordinates described. Participants include a healthy control group (PET, n=12) with within-group contrasts; patient behavioral data are additional but do not negate the PET within-group activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of verbal fluency (an executive function) in ASD and controls, so it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts/activations reported at the individual level), I9 (clinical sample allowed), and I10 (results described in the text). However, the paper does not present a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; analyses are reported as individual-level voxelwise maps and ROI-derived measures (percent signal change and activation volume within a left frontal ROI) and group statistics on those ROI measures. Therefore it fails I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/region-based/group-summary measures reported without a group-level voxelwise activation map). Because I7 is not met and E3 is triggered, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based O-15 PET study with within-group voxelwise contrasts (navigation test vs control) using whole-brain SPM analyses and reported stereotactic coordinates. The navigation task as implemented engages executive processes (authors report recruitment of prefrontal regions associated with planning and spatial working memory), so it reasonably falls within established executive-function domains (planning, working memory). Results include group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and coordinate reports. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm that directly probes inhibitory control/selection (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain cluster-corrected results and a basal-ganglia ROI volume of interest) and within-group task contrasts (isolated index-finger vs full-hand; rest vs movements). Participants were a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=10). Results are reported in the text with voxelwise/statistical mapping and anatomical localization. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an FDG-PET study using an auditory continuous performance task (CPT) and thus meets I5 (PET, task-based) and I6 (vigilance falls within the executive domain), and includes an eligible participant group (healthy adults) satisfying I9. However, the paper does not report any within-group task-evoked activation contrasts (no task>baseline or similar within-group statistical map) and instead presents interregional metabolic associativity (correlational/connectivity) analyses and voxelwise correlational maps. Therefore it fails I8 (no within-group task contrast) and I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical activation map qualifying as a task activation). This meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only connectivity/associativity analyses without a task activation map). Conclusion: EXCLUDE (meets E4).

This study used PET to measure changes in striatal dopamine binding and reported behavioral executive-function task performance, but it did not report any task-evoked, group-level voxelwise activation maps linking an executive task to PET/fMRI activation. Although this is a PET study of executive-function-related cognition (Stockings of Cambridge and Wisconsin Card Sorting Test) and thus meets I5 and I6 (and I9, as clinical participants are included), it does NOT report any task-evoked, within-group voxelwise activation maps. This study used PET to measure dopamine D2 receptor binding at rest and correlated binding values with neuropsychological test scores. This study used PET to measure striatal D2 receptor availability at rest and related these receptor binding values to behavioral performance on executive tasks (spatial working memory, Tower of London). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (tasks are established executive domains: working memory and planning) and I9 (participant group is an eligible within-group sample). This is an empirical PET study using a task-based working memory paradigm (delayed non-match-to-sample), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The article reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 (spatial normalization, smoothing, voxelwise linear regression, and thresholding), with group-level task-versus-baseline contrasts and tables/figures of regional activations (main effects and group-by-task interactions). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study correlates [11C]FLB 457 binding (a receptor-binding measure) with WCST performance but does not report any task-evoked PET activation maps or a within-group task contrast (task vs baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study that included an executive task), I6 (WCST falls within executive function/cognitive flexibility), I9 (within-group sample qualifies: healthy volunteers). The study is excluded because it reports only between-group voxelwise contrasts (marijuana users vs controls) and does not present any within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., a group-level Conflict vs No-Conflict one-sample/group main effect) for either participant group. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only between-group contrasts reported with no within-group task activation maps). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based PET study of executive function using a Stroop inhibition paradigm), I6 (task falls within executive domains - inhibition/cognitive control), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM99 and whole-brain post-hoc analyses), I10 (whole-brain results/coordinates described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (although clinical participants are allowed, I9 requires a within-group contrast to be reported for at least one group, which is not present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This PET study relates resting-state cerebral metabolism to performance on a Continuous Performance Test (vigilance), but did not acquire task-evoked (task-based) PET/fMRI activation maps. Inclusion met: I6 (task used—the CPT—fits executive domain: vigilance). Inclusion not met: I5 (imaging was not task-based/ no task-evoked PET), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast / task activation vs baseline within the imaging data), I9 (no within-group task activation contrast reported for any group). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analyses focus on predefined ROIs/metabolic rates rather than reporting voxelwise task activation maps) and E5 (no within-group task activation contrasts; only correlations/regressions and group × metabolism interactions reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study does not provide the required task-evoked, voxelwise within-group activation maps and must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based auditory continuous performance test (CPT) — a vigilance/attention executive-domain task — with healthy adult participants. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses are reported (Task vs Rest and Rest vs Task contrasts) and coordinates/figures/tables of activations/deactivations are provided. The study reports within-group task contrasts (Active minus Rest) and provides voxelwise PET statistical maps and coordinates used to guide electrophysiological analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive function activations.

This is a PET pharmacology study measuring dopamine D2 receptor occupancy and relating occupancy to behavioral performance on working memory and learning tasks. Although the cognitive tasks fall within executive function domains (working memory, learning), the study does not report any task-evoked whole-brain, voxelwise neuroimaging activation maps or group-level task contrast images. The PET data are used to quantify receptor binding (occupancy), not to measure task-related brain activation. Therefore it fails to meet imaging-specific inclusion criteria requiring a task-based fMRI/PET activation analysis and whole-brain voxelwise results. Full text is complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report task-evoked, voxelwise neuroimaging activation maps or within-group task contrasts. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (study reports ROI-based PET kinetic analyses and region-wise time-activity/kinetic results rather than voxelwise task-evoked activation maps). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (study is not a task-based fMRI/PET activation study — PET was used for molecular FDOPA kinetics at rest, not to measure task-evoked activations), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast in imaging data — CPT behavioral measures were collected but not used to generate within-group task activation maps), I10 (not applicable — no whole-brain task results reported in tables/figures as activation maps). This is an empirical PET study using a task-based auditory oddball paradigm that targets attentional control/vigilance (an established executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (within-group contrasts B–A for controls and patients) with whole-brain spatial normalization and cluster-based inference, meeting the requirement for voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participant groups include healthy controls and a clinical schizophrenia sample; within-group contrasts are reported for at least one group. Although the PET field-of-view emphasized lower brain regions, partial-brain acquisition is acceptable per criteria and analyses were voxelwise. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study used FDG-PET during an auditory continuous performance task (a vigilance/executive task) but reports voxelwise interregional metabolic associativity (connectivity) analyses rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked activation contrast (task vs baseline). Inclusion satisfied: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (task = vigilance), and I10 (voxelwise results clearly described). Inclusion NOT satisfied: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented), I8 (no within-group task activation contrast reported), I9 (while clinical groups are included, the required within-group activation contrast is missing). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without a task activation map). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based visual working memory paradigm (an executive-function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with within-group task>rest contrasts for young and older groups, and results are presented in tables/figures with coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical PET study with task-based paradigms that probe verbal working memory (listening/encoding word pairs and immediate verbal repetition), which falls within executive function domains (working memory). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM with random-effects models and FWE correction, and presents within-group contrasts (task vs rest) and main effects of task; results are described voxelwise (clusters, local maxima) in the text and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This PET study used a task-based Stroop paradigm (executive function — cognitive control/inhibition) and reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps derived from NPAIRS/CVA (canonical eigenimages/statistical parametric maps) with cluster/threshold criteria. The paper provides within-group task contrasts for both patients and controls, and reports locations and statistics for activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study (H2 15O) that examines cognitive processes during go game tasks. The tasks include territorial planning (planning — an established executive function) and checkmate judgment; Task 1 explicitly maps to the planning domain. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (group-level contrasts, thresholded and corrected) and presents within-group subtraction contrasts (task vs baseline and correct vs incorrect) for both professional and amateur groups. Results are described in the text and figures. Participants include nonclinical adult groups, which are acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations and should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study (with concurrent electrophysiology) using an auditory continuous performance test (CPT), which is a vigilance/attention executive function paradigm. The study reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses contrasting Active (task) versus Rest (within-group contrast) across 12 subjects, with whole-brain coverage and reported coordinates/tables of significant activation and deactivation foci. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activation meta-analysis and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

Exclusion reasons: E5 and E4. The study reports resting-state FDG-PET group comparisons (MA users vs controls) and correlations between resting metabolism and WCST performance, but it does not report any task-evoked, within-group activation contrast (no imaging was acquired during the WCST). Therefore it meets E5 (only between-group contrasts/no within-group task activation) and E4 (resting metabolic scan without a task-activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I9 (participant groups allowed) and I10 (results reported with voxel coordinates/images). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET paradigm for executive function), I6 (task-based imaging within executive domains not performed), I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), and I8 (no within-group task contrast reported). Full text appears complete.

The study uses PET molecular imaging of striatal DAT binding and behavioral cognitive tests; it does not report task-evoked, within-group PET/fMRI activation contrasts or group-level voxelwise activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (behavioral tasks used are within executive-function domains: working memory, verbal fluency). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET activation study — PET measured DAT binding at rest), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported as imaging data), I9 (conditional on I8; no within-group imaging contrast), I10 (no whole-brain task activation results reported). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 apply. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED because it fails to meet multiple required inclusion criteria (notably I5, I7, and I8).

This is an empirical PET study of executive function using task-based paradigms (dual-task and integration) that probe central executive processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM99 analyses (fixed- and random-effects), with whole-brain contrasts (e.g., dual − [auditory + visual], integration − [auditory + visual]) and lists activation coordinates and thresholding—satisfying voxelwise, whole-brain reporting. Within-group task contrasts are provided, and healthy adult participants were tested. Results are reported in text, tables/figures, and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Although this is an empirical PET study with voxelwise, within-group task contrasts, it does not assess a task that clearly falls within the review's specified executive-function domains. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses / t-maps), I8 (within-group contrast: control vs test), I9 (healthy volunteer participant group), I10 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 — the task is an implicit serial reaction time (sequential motor learning) paradigm targeting procedural/sequence learning and motor systems; it is not clearly one of the specified executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore the study is excluded. Full text is complete and methods/results/discussion are present.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title, metadata, and abstract only (fulltext_incomplete=true). From the abstract we can verify I5 (task-based neuroimaging of an executive function — updating), I6 (task falls within executive domains — updating/working memory), and I10 (task-evoked activations are described in the text). However, the provided content does not allow verification of I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map) or I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported) because methods/results detail and full article are not available. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are demonstrably met based on the abstract alone. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, I must exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

The paper reports task-based fMRI (Go/no-go, Simon, Switch) probing inhibition and cognitive flexibility (executive function domains). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (GBAM, permutation-based voxelwise and cluster-level inference), within-group task contrasts for adolescents and adults, and reports coordinate tables and whole-brain regression maps. Participants include developmental samples (adolescents and adults). Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly assesses executive functions (response inhibition via go/no-go and cognitive flexibility via WCST) using task-based paradigms and within-group contrasts. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise/pixel-wise statistical maps (two-way ANOVA, pixel-wise significance, Talairach coordinates) despite partial-brain (limited slice) coverage, which still meets the review's allowance for partial-brain voxelwise analyses. Results include within-group contrasts (no-go vs. go; shift-related vs. baseline) and peak coordinates/figures. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, an established executive-function paradigm (working memory, set-shifting/cognitive flexibility). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t tests) with multiple within-group contrasts (A-HLB, B-HLB, C-HLB, A–C, A–B, B–C), and provides coordinate tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of motor response inhibition (go/no-go and stop tasks), which are established executive function (inhibition) paradigms. The paper reports within-group generic activation maps for controls and patients and group-level voxelwise ANCOVA comparisons; whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and peak coordinates/tables are reported. Although slice coverage is partial (14 non-contiguous planes), the analyses are voxelwise and qualify under partial-brain acquisition. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms targeting executive functions (WCST for cognitive flexibility and an n-back for working memory). Group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported (event-related transient activation tied to dimensional changes; 2-back vs 0-back blocked contrast), with voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach coordinates provided. Although slice coverage was partial (four contiguous slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, which meets the protocol allowance for partial-brain acquisition. Participants were healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive functions. It uses multiple established executive tasks (working memory — verbal and spatial; inhibition — stop, go/no-go, flanker), reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., no-go vs oddball, stop vs oddball, incongruent vs congruent, WM vs control), and conducts group-level random-effects (SPM) whole-brain analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates/tables. Participants are a human within-group sample (healthy adults). The paper includes full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (inhibition) using a go/no-go paradigm. It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., no-go vs infrequent-go; infrequent-go vs frequent-go) analyzed with SPM2 and thresholded across the whole brain, with results presented in tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition using an emotional linguistic go/no-go paradigm, which falls squarely within executive function (inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM maps, FDR-corrected results) and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., NegativeNoGo vs NeutralNoGo, NegativeNoGo vs NegativeGo). Results are reported as statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-go), addressing executive control. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample voxelwise t-tests with cluster correction) and reports coordinates/tables and figures. At least one within-group task contrast is presented (STOPS: successful No-go > ongoing Go trials). Participant sample (n=42 healthy adults) is acceptable per inclusion rules. The manuscript contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections (full article content present). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This paper is a meta-analysis of published fMRI studies (an ALE coordinate-based meta-analysis) and does not present original participant-level fMRI or PET data or group-level voxelwise task activation maps. Exclusion E6 applies: it is a meta-analysis without original human neuroimaging data. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (addresses an executive function domain — response inhibition). I10 (reports whole-brain results/coordinates in text/tables as part of the meta-analysis). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an original fMRI or PET study reporting new primary data), I7 (does not provide an original group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map from participant data), I8 (the paper itself does not report a within-group task contrast from original data; it aggregates contrasts from included studies). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded per the review’s exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI Go/No-Go study using a within-group contrast (Do Swallow vs Don’t Swallow) and clearly reports voxelwise single-subject analyses; thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition/Go–No-Go), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (healthy adult group), and I10 (results described in text/figures). However, the group-level inference was performed via an ROI-based analysis (counting activated voxels within anatomically defined ROIs and conducting pairwise t-tests on those counts). The paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (i.e., no voxelwise group map or voxelwise group contrast results are presented), so it fails I7. Because no voxelwise group-level activation maps are reported and the group analysis is ROI-only, this meets Exclusion E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise group results). Therefore the study is excluded.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task assessing executive function), I6 (planning task within executive domains). Inclusion criteria not confirmed / therefore not met based on available text: I7 (cannot verify presence of group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses or maps), I8 (cannot confirm a within-group task contrast reported), I10 (cannot confirm whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). Exclusion criteria met: none (no evidence of ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Because key methodological details and voxelwise within-group results cannot be verified from the provided incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text access.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (executive function) that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (no-go vs. go; incongruent vs. congruent; incompatible vs. compatible). The manuscript includes methods, results, figures, and tables describing random-effects SPM99 analyses with FDR correction and coordinates, and reports behavioral and brain–behavior correlations. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported in the main text and figures/tables, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly assesses an executive function domain (verbal working memory using a 2-back vs 0-back paradigm). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM2 analyses (group-level tests and coordinates), subject-level within-subject contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) and at least one within-group one-sample/ANCOVA (male group interaction analysis). Results are reported with tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and should be included.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of inhibition of imitative responses and reports within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and brain activations in prefrontal and parietal regions. Based on the available abstract/metadata it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results described). However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata present) and does not allow verification that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map was reported (I7). Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included at this time. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Recommend obtaining the full article to confirm voxelwise whole-brain analyses.

This empirical fMRI study uses two canonical executive-function tasks (N-back for working memory and Go/No-go for inhibition), reports within-group GLM analyses and group-level voxelwise t maps (registered to MNI space), and presents whole-brain activation cluster results and coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI on executive function), I6 (tasks are working memory and inhibition), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts and group t maps), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as maps/clusters). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of response inhibition (go/no-go) using emotional and letter stimuli, which is an established executive function domain (inhibition). It includes within-group, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (no-go vs go) with whole-brain composite maps (Talairach-transformed), and reports cluster activations and coordinates/BA labels. Partial-brain slice coverage is present (14 slices), but the analysis is voxelwise and therefore acceptable per criteria. Participants are a within-group healthy sample, and at least one within-group task contrast is reported. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of executive function (set shifting/cognitive flexibility) in healthy adults. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99 group-averaged t maps) and ROI analyses, and presents within-group contrasts (e.g., targets vs novels; target-shift vs target-maintain). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided, and voxelwise task activation maps/analyses are clearly described. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), enabling extraction of within-group task activation results for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task switching) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group contrasts (mixed-task vs single-task; task-switch vs task-repeat). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, indicating completeness. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. The study provides voxelwise random-effects ANOVAs and ROI analyses derived from whole-brain results, satisfying meta-analysis requirements.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes a go/no-go response inhibition task (an established executive function domain: inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (contrasts such as no-go vs. go and nine vs. one stimuli) using random-effects statistics and provides tables/figures with coordinates and cluster thresholds (p<.001 uncorrected). Participant groups (children and adults) each have within-group contrasts reported. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This empirical, task-based fMRI study uses a Go/No-Go inhibitory control paradigm (an established executive function domain) and reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (Press for all letters except X − Press for X) analyzed with random-effects whole-brain SPM99 analyses and corrected thresholds. Whole-brain results (left cerebellum) and voxel coordinates for frontal ROIs are reported (cluster coordinates and statistics), satisfying voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps. Participants are an eligible group (young adults), and the paper includes complete methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a go/no-go paradigm that probes inhibition (an executive function). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (no-go vs. go), whole-brain acquisition and group-level permutation-based voxel/cluster maps, with coordinates and figures. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using a Go/No-go task (response inhibition) in healthy adults. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level analyses (SPM multisubject GLM) with explicit within-group contrasts (Go vs baseline; No-go vs baseline; No-go vs Go) and provides tables/figures of peak coordinates and statistical maps. The task falls within the executive function domain (inhibition). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go), which is an established executive function (inhibition). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level task analyses (GNG vs. fixation) with multiple-comparison correction and provides Talairach coordinates and figures. At least one within-group/main-effect task contrast (GNG vs fixation) is reported (collapsed across subjects), and results are described in text, tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a stop-signal paradigm that probes inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (successful and failed inhibition; main effect of inhibition against implicit baseline) in a within-subject design of healthy volunteers. Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM and permutation-based CAMBA) with cluster-level inference and peak MNI coordinates reported for right inferior frontal gyrus activations; plasma-level correlations were also conducted within a brain mask. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and reports within-group activation contrasts). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (executive function: cognitive flexibility). It reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (e.g., negative feedback minus control) with random-effects T-statistic images and whole-brain thresholding and cluster correction; results are reported in tables and figures. The study thus meets criteria for fMRI task-based executive-function assessment (I5), task domain (cognitive flexibility) (I6), whole-brain voxelwise analysis (I7), within-group task contrasts (I8), acceptable participant group (healthy adults) (I9), and reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM99) including within-group contrasts (n-back vs 0-back) for both depressed patients and healthy controls, with coordinates, cluster maps, and statistical thresholds provided. Although acquisition used 14 axial slices (partial coverage), the analyses were voxelwise and thus meet the partial-brain allowance. Clinical and control participant groups are included. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (audiospatial n-back), which is an established executive function. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (3-back vs 1-back; 2-back vs 1-back) using voxelwise two-tailed t-tests and voxelwise statistical maps; Talairach coordinates and tables/figures of whole-brain activations are provided. Partial brain coverage is acceptable per criteria and the analysis is voxelwise. Participants are a healthy adult group (within-group contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study examining planning (Tower of London), an executive function. It reports group-level voxelwise t-maps (t>6), Talairach-averaged activation maps, and tables of activation, and performs within-group contrasts (task vs baseline, parametric difficulty effects and ANOVAs). Partial slice coverage was used but analyses were voxelwise and group-level, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The paper also reports functional connectivity but additionally provides standard task-evoked activation results. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts relevant to executive function. The Go/No-Go task assesses response inhibition (an established executive function domain). The manuscript reports within-group contrasts (No-Go > Go; Reward > No-Reward; Loss > No-Loss) analyzed using SPM2 with second-level random-effects voxelwise analyses and cluster reporting, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable). Results are reported in figures and tables (coordinates referenced). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided content is complete.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-go) that assesses executive function (inhibition and working memory). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects statistical maps (corrected P≤0.05) and provides whole-brain coverage for many subjects, with within-group contrasts (Go and No-go main effects, No-go>Go, conjunctions, paired t-tests). Results are reported as tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a go/no-go inhibitory control paradigm (executive function). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (cognitive minus reference) for participant groups and also reports exploratory whole-brain voxelwise between-group analyses (Table 3), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise results. The task falls within the inhibition domain, and results are reported at group level with coordinates and tables. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI task study of cognitive control (Stroop task) with task-based paradigm and group-level voxelwise spatial F maps reported. It includes within-group contrasts (instruction-related: color naming vs word reading; response-related: incongruent vs congruent), reports group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates for activations, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Participant details are reported. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of inhibition using a go/no-go task (meets I5, I6) and reports within-group task contrasts (go/no-go vs baseline) in healthy adults (meets I8 and I9) and presents voxelwise results in figures/text (meets I10). However, the fMRI analysis was restricted to preselected regions of interest (motor cortex and preSMA) with Bonferroni correction applied for those ROIs, i.e. the reported voxelwise results are confined to a priori regions rather than a whole-brain voxelwise analysis. This violates the requirement for a whole-brain (or at least not ROI-restricted) voxelwise task map (I7) and therefore falls under exclusion E3 (ROI/small-volume-restricted reporting with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise map). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cued task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility/cognitive control). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., cues vs implicit baseline, targets vs implicit baseline, cues vs targets), with whole-brain results reported (tables/figures/coordinates). Participants were healthy adults; reporting is sufficient for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of antisaccade performance (a response inhibition task within the executive function domain). The authors report group-level, voxelwise statistical maps using SPM2 (whole-brain analyses, threshold P<0.001) and present within-group contrasts (antisaccade vs control) for both normal controls and schizophrenia patients. The sample includes clinical and control groups, and whole-brain results are described in the text (with reported activated regions). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). All required inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the Stroop (inhibition) paradigm (executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group SPM analyses (I-C, I-N, C-N) with cluster maps and tables of significant clusters/coordinates and describes within-group contrasts for younger and older groups. Methods detail whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise statistical mapping; results include group-level task activation maps and coordinates. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function with within-group, whole-brain voxelwise results and reports coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses and multiple within-group contrasts (1-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 1-back). Results are presented as statistical maps, figures, and tables of coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly assesses inhibition (executive control) using two established tasks (manual Stroop and an imitation-inhibition task). Group-level, voxelwise analyses were reported (SPM{z} group maps, thresholding and cluster-size criterion) with whole-brain coverage and coordinates/tables provided. Key within-group contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) are reported for each task. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts present). Results are reported as whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables, meeting reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (set-shifting), an established executive function (cognitive flexibility) paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (thresholding, cluster correction) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., receiving negative feedback vs control; matching after negative feedback vs control) for both Parkinson’s patients and matched controls. Results are reported in tables and described in the text. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain fMRI with within-group contrasts; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is provided and appears complete.

This fMRI study (working memory tasks) meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for younger and older groups), and I9 (participant groups reported). However, the full text presents results focused on a scene-selective ROI and modulation indices and does not describe any group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps or voxelwise analyses. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion criterion I7 (requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a go/no-go inhibitory control task (an executive function: inhibition). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (no-go > go) for controls, unaffected siblings, and ADHD participants, with whole-brain analyses (one-sample t-tests) and reported coordinate tables/figures. These satisfy the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive-function fMRI, whole-brain voxelwise results, and within-group task contrasts. Participant groups (clinical and developmental samples) are acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, empirical human fMRI data present). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses using SPM2 (maps and Talairach coordinates are provided) and explicit within-group task contrasts (1-back and 2-back vs 0-back; conjunction analyses). Results are reported for both participant groups (controls and cocaine abusers) and include coordinate tables and statistical maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task) that reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses in 20 healthy adults. The paper provides group-level statistical mapping (GBAM), voxelwise SSQratio maps, cluster-level inference, coordinates and figures/tables for whole-brain activation foci, and within-group contrasts (successful vs unsuccessful stops; unsuccessful stops vs go trials). All inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Full text provided is limited to title/abstract/metadata only. The abstract indicates a PET GO/NO-GO task (inhibition), and reports task-minus-control and task-minus-task rCBF change images, which meets I5 (PET task-based) and I6 (executive function - inhibition) and I8 (within-group task contrasts). This is a task-based fMRI study (N-Back and AX-CPT) probing executive functions (working memory and inhibition) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level ANOVAs and planned contrasts, with tables of activated regions (coordinates) and figures showing whole-brain activation patterns and within-group effects (e.g., load-related and cue-type effects). Within-group task contrasts and planned contrasts for each group are described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, tasks, image acquisition, voxelwise analyses), Results (behavioral and imaging tables/figures), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10; no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical ASL fMRI study reporting within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level task activation maps for two executive-function tasks (visual sustained attention/vigilance and 2-back working memory). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results (cluster tables and coordinates), and discussion, and reports task-versus-rest contrasts using random-effects voxelwise analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study reports an event-related fMRI GO/NO-GO task assessing response inhibition (an executive function), with group-level task-evoked activations described for NO-GO and GO responses. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (Go/No-go), which is an established executive function domain. This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive control / cognitive flexibility). This is an empirical PET activation study of planning (Tower of London), an executive function domain. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that manipulates executive demand (two-back vs one-back; source vs item memory) and explicitly investigates executive control. This is a task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition), an established executive function paradigm. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go), which falls squarely within executive function (inhibition). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) — an executive function domain. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. This is an original, task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task switching using Stroop/reverse-Stroop), reporting group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses of within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; Stroop, RS-Early, RS-Late) with whole-brain coverage and tables/figures of results. This is an event-related fMRI study of executive control processes (Go/No-go inhibition, oddball target detection, response selection). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task switching) that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses.
