Although acquisition uses limited (14-slice) coverage, analyses are voxelwise and thus meet the partial-brain allowance. A clinical participant group (non-demented ALS) is included and within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based executive function paradigm (counting Stroop; inhibition). Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (mixed-effects; thresholded Z statistical images) and report coordinates/tables and figures. Within-group I–N (interference minus neutral) contrasts were performed for each condition (Trp and Placebo), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5-I10). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures; not truncated. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., untrained vs trained, trained vs untrained, fact retrieval vs number matching) using SPM random-effects analyses with tables/figures. Tasks involve significant working-memory and planning/executive demands (complex mental multiplication) and the paper explicitly interprets activations in terms of working memory and executive processes. Participants are healthy adults and contrasts are within-group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop task (inhibition/selective attention), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM group activation maps) and provides within-group contrasts (Stroop activation vs. rest) for both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients, with tables of coordinates and figures. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group contrasts are present, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visual N-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (parametric working-memory load; corrected voxelwise thresholding) and within-group task contrasts (parametric increase contrasts and mean activation versus baseline), with results presented in figures/tables. Participants (chronic smokers) are an eligible group and within-group contrasts are reported for them. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (attention-switching/working memory) with healthy adult participants. It reports within-group, voxelwise group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests and repeated-measures voxelwise ANOVAs) and whole-brain activation maps (with cluster-corrected thresholds). Tasks fall clearly within working memory/executive domains, and results are reported across the brain (voxelwise maps and ROI follow-ups). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that probes working memory (an established executive function domain) via structured vs. unstructured digit sequences. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; whole-brain FDR thresholding; coordinate reporting) and presents within-group task contrasts (structured > unstructured during encoding and delay). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in text, figures and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI task-based study with within-group voxelwise analyses (object change vs no change) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain coordinates. However, the paradigm investigates visual object and spatial discrimination/perception and medial temporal lobe involvement, not an established executive function or cognitive control domain. Although the authors speculate about short-term visual working memory, the task involves simultaneous comparison with minimal retention and was explicitly designed to minimize declarative memory demands; it does not operationalize working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation as defined by the meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met, despite I7, I8, I9 and I10 being satisfied. Full text is complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Abstract indicates an empirical PET study of verbal working memory (meets I5, I6), uses task and control conditions consistent with a within-group task contrast (meets I8), and includes human participants (meets I9). However, I cannot verify from the provided content whether a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map was reported (I7) or whether results are reported in the forms acceptable per I10. Because the full text (methods/results) is not available, key inclusion criteria (particularly I7) cannot be confirmed and exclusion via inability to verify is necessary pending retrieval of the full article.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates a task-based 18FDG-PET working memory study (so I5, I6) with within-group contrasts implied (I8) and includes clinical groups (I9). However, I cannot verify whether group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps were reported (I7) or whether results/coordinates sufficient for inclusion were provided (I10). Because the complete methods/results are not available, I cannot confirm the critical whole-brain voxelwise evidence required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone, but inability to verify I7 and I10 prevents confident inclusion. Therefore I exclude this record pending access to the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly investigates planning, an established executive function domain (planning). It uses a task-based within-subject design (Final Goal vs Immediate Goal) and reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM; cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates/figures described. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (planning), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (color-word and emotion-word Stroop tasks involve inhibition/selective attention). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (incongruent-minus-neutral; negative-minus-neutral) and group-level voxelwise statistical maps (paired t tests, thresholded via Monte Carlo simulations/AlphaSim), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported activations. Tasks fall within the inhibition/executive control domain. Participants are a within-group sample. Results include voxelwise group maps (figures, ROI and whole-brain cluster-based maps). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (object and spatial delayed-recognition), which is an established executive-function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (mapwise contrasts and thresholded activation maps) and provides within-group task contrasts vs. fixation and object vs. spatial contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (mapwise, regional, ROI analyses) and Discussion, indicating completeness. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cued task-switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). Methods report group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts (random-effects t-tests, contrast maps transformed to z-scores) and selection of ROIs from whole-brain contrasts; contrasts include within-group task comparisons (e.g., combined conditions vs null, switch vs repeat, left vs right responses). Participants are healthy adults and within-group analyses are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical methods paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based counting Stroop (executive control/inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (incongruent > congruent contrast), provides group-level within-group activation maps for both patient and healthy groups, and reports coordinates/figures. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation maps and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET task-based study of executive function (working memory updating) that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM95) comparing a within-group task contrast (variable-target vs fixed-target). Results are reported with Talairach coordinates, figures, and a table of activations. Participants are a healthy adult sample. Therefore the study meets I5 (PET task assessing executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group qualifies), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This PET study reports voxelwise, group-level task activation contrasts comparing simultaneous interpreting (SI) vs shadowing within eight professional interpreters, using SPM and whole-brain subtraction analyses. The SI task clearly engages verbal working memory and related cognitive-control processes (described in the paper), placing it within established executive-function domains (working memory/controlled retrieval). Group-level within-subject contrasts (SI vs shadowing; direction contrasts) are reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level inference, satisfying whole-brain, task-evoked mapping requirements. The participant sample is acceptable, and results are reported in text/figures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility) that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (searchlight maps normalized and subjected to second-level voxelwise statistics) and within-group contrasts/testing of decoding accuracy against chance. Participants are healthy adults. The report includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory with distraction (executive function domain). The paper reports task-based fMRI analyses (I5) using a working memory paradigm (I6). The methods describe whole-brain activation maps and voxelwise linear contrasts (delay1 vs baseline) used to define ROIs and secondary uniform-threshold whole-brain analyses, indicating group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7). Multiple within-group task contrasts and within-subject comparisons (e.g., delay1 vs baseline, face/scene vs face/face) are reported (I8). The sample is a within-group healthy adult cohort (I9) and whole-brain results are described in the text and analyses (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise surface/volume analyses and contrasts (e.g., EAR > NO-MEMORY, EAR > EYE) that are within-group task contrasts. Whole-brain analyses and statistical maps are described and thresholding/clusters reported; supplemental data and coordinates are available. Participants are healthy adult subjects. The report also includes methods, results, and discussion (full article content provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the paper reports behavioral group comparisons but provides no within-group task-evoked whole-brain activation maps or voxelwise task contrasts for any group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 — the tasks are within an executive function domain (working memory). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no fMRI or PET task-based activation data are reported in this paper; the authors used behavioural versions of tasks previously used in fMRI studies), I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation maps are provided), I8 (no within-group task activation contrasts are reported), I9 (requires a within-group task contrast for at least one participant group — not met), I10 (not applicable because no whole-brain imaging results are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide the task-evoked neuroimaging activation maps required for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (face recognition within a working memory/search task), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses: voxelwise thresholds (Z>3.09), counts of significant voxels across six participants, Talairach coordinates, and regional volumes—i.e., whole-brain activation results reported as coordinates/figures. Within-group task contrasts are reported (targets vs nonrepeated distracters; repeated distracters vs nonrepeated distracters), and behavioral within-group results are also presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included).

This fMRI study directly investigates working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based retro-cueing paradigm and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked analyses. The paper includes whole-brain statistical comparisons (FDR-corrected), ROI and time-course analyses, and a table of coordinates for network activations. Within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., cue vs implicit baseline; switch vs stay), and analyses are conducted on healthy participant groups. Results include voxelwise maps and coordinate tables, satisfying requirements for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI task study of response selection (executive/cognitive control). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level SPM contrasts (e.g., free selection vs externally specified, action vs colour, main effect of task vs rest) with whole-brain inference and tables of coordinates. The paradigm probes executive selection processes (selection/choice), satisfying executive-domain criteria. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=12). Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and coordinate tables/figures, indicating complete full text for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a working memory task (executive function domain) with whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group analyses reported. The manuscript includes full methods, results (within-group task>rest and stage-specific contrasts), and coordinates/cluster statistics, meeting all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/interaction with retrieval), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., Strong > Weak and Weak > Strong), I9 (healthy adult participant group; within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Did NOT meet I6: the experimental task is an associative episodic recognition memory task, not one of the listed established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); although the paper examines cognitive-control-related regions (ACC, DLPFC), the primary task does not fall within the required EF task categories. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI (overt word-generation paradigms) using voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. Evidence: (1) fMRI acquisition and GLM analyses are described in detail; (2) tasks (categorical, alphabetical, semantic word generation) map onto executive processes (initiation/controlled retrieval and cognitive control of language production); (3) voxelwise statistical maps (t- and F-contrasts) and mixed-effects analyses are reported; (4) within-group contrasts (paradigm vs baseline per session and mixed-effect across sessions/subjects) are explicitly tested; (5) participants are human healthy volunteers. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation that includes a sustained visual attention (vigilance) task and directly reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level contrasts (task>baseline, ER>VA, VA>ER) using SPM99 with tables/figures of coordinates. This satisfies inclusion: I5 (fMRI task-based study), I6 (vigilance – an executive function domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Tables, References). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Continuous Performance Task (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM analyses (random-effects t-maps for CPT vs control) used to select voxels/VOIs and to compare within-group activation patterns; although analyses focus on frontal mask, the procedure used voxelwise statistics (partial-brain voxelwise analysis is acceptable). Within-group contrasts are reported for control and patient groups. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and matched controls. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

While this is an event-related fMRI study using an anti-/pro-saccade task (an inhibition-based executive function), and it reports within-group contrasts and Talairach coordinates, it does not present a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the main event-related analyses. The authors used single-subject localizer voxelwise maps to define ROIs and then extracted ROI time courses for group ANOVAs; the primary analyses are ROI-based/ROI-extracted rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map. Therefore Inclusion criteria I5, I6, I8, I9, and I10 are met, but I7 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) is not met. This study effectively reports ROI-based analyses without the required group-level voxelwise activation maps, meeting Exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI methods paper using visual stimulation (flashing checkerboards) and simulations to compare GLM modeling approaches. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts and group maps, so it meets I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as maps/statistics). However it does NOT assess executive function or cognitive control tasks and does not use tasks within established executive-function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, flexibility), so it fails I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (novel AX-CPT) in healthy adults. The full text reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects second-level maps, FDR-corrected) and within-group task contrasts (reward expectancy, verbal/spatial bias, all-tasks vs rest). It also reports coordinates and figures for activations and includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function) that reports group-level, voxelwise SPM2 analyses and group maps with stereotactic peak coordinates. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (encoding, delay, retrieval; delay-period activity contrasted against baseline), includes healthy participant data, and presents whole-brain voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical article) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based 2-back verbal working memory paradigm (an executive function), with group-level, voxelwise SPM99 whole-brain analyses reported (coordinates and cluster sizes). The paper reports within-group task-related rCBF changes (2-back vs reference) and correlations of performance with rCBF, meeting the requirement for within-group contrasts. Results are reported as voxelwise maps/coordinates. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based mental rotation paradigm that explicitly probes visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 random-effects group analyses (one-sample t-tests for within-group activation maps, two-sample and paired t-tests for between-group contrasts) and provides tables/figures with coordinates. The primary within-group contrast (mental rotation vs passive viewing/control) is reported for each group. Participant characteristics and hormone-state manipulations are detailed but do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are present). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study examines inhibition (a core executive function) with task-based fMRI and within-subject contrasts (INT vs COV), and reports behavioral, ERP, and fMRI results. However, the fMRI analysis is ROI-based (AROI parcellation) with AROI-level statistics rather than group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/inhibition), I6 (task falls within inhibition domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (acceptable participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an emotional Stroop paradigm that requires participants to inhibit word meaning and report ink color (an inhibition/cognitive-control executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (negative vs neutral; positive vs neutral), provides cluster-thresholding and coordinates/tables, and extracts within-group activation maps and ROIs. Multiple participant groups are included and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task), I6 (inhibition/cognitive control task), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task (antisaccade/prosaccade delayed saccade paradigm) that probes inhibition and volitional response generation—core executive functions (inhibition/response control). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2), whole-brain activation maps and cluster-level results (tables and figures), and within-group contrasts (e.g., standard antisaccade vs fixation; delayed task phases). Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Results are reported as coordinates and SPMs with full methods, results, and discussion. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study uses a task-based continuous performance test (CPT), which falls under vigilance/attentional executive functions. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (task vs baseline and degraded vs non-degraded contrasts), with whole-brain voxelwise inference constrained by anatomical masks and tables of peak coordinates and figures. Within-subject contrasts were generated and entered into second-level (within-group and between-group) analyses; task main effects and condition (degradation) effects are modelled and reported. Results include coordinate tables and activation maps and psycho-physiological interaction analyses, so the paper provides task activation maps (voxelwise) and within-group contrasts for at least one group. Participants include clinical groups (schizophrenia) and healthy controls. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of decision-making that explicitly tests cognitive control/conflict (ACC, DLPFC) during moral dilemmas. The task is task-based and requires inhibition/cognitive control (overriding prepotent emotional responses), meeting the executive-function domain (inhibition/cognitive control). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain and ROI-constrained contrasts (e.g., high-RT vs low-RT; utilitarian vs nonutilitarian) reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction. Within-group task contrasts are reported and RT was controlled in comparisons. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented in the full article (text, figures, and reported thresholds/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual-spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects ANOVAs, corrected cluster thresholds), within-group task contrasts (main effect of time maps for each age group; long vs short delay contrasts within groups), and provides coordinates/figures/tables of activations. Participant groups include children, adolescents, and adults. The paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, nor solely between-group contrasts. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory and spatial attention within the same subjects. The abstract describes group-level conjunction and double-subtraction analyses that identify distributed activations across frontal and parietal regions, indicating voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses and within-group contrasts. These features satisfy inclusion criteria for an executive-function (working memory) task-based fMRI study with within-group contrasts and group-level voxelwise results. I cannot verify full article contents (methods, results tables/coordinates, or figures) because only the abstract/metadata were provided; therefore fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are apparent from the abstract. Inclusion criteria applied are listed below.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study that explicitly investigates a cognitive control strategy (‘reality checking’) during anticipation of emotional stimuli. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses and within-group contrasts (e.g., negative vs neutral; unknown vs neutral) with Talairach-transformed whole-brain results reported in tables/figures. Participants are human (healthy adults). Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so it appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (an executive function), reports within-group contrasts (Order vs baseline) in healthy adults, and meets I5, I6, I8, I9, and I10. However, all reported group-level results are ROI-restricted (analyses conducted on predefined ROIs with ROI-based statistics reported) and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-activation map is presented. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis) is not met and exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results) applies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based flanker/ANT variant that probes executive function (inhibition/cognitive control). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (group-averaged activation maps and random-effects contrast maps with FDR thresholding) and extracts regional hemodynamic timecourses. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent > congruent/low-arousal; high-arousal > low-arousal within groups), and results are presented across both neurotypical and autism participant groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and provides coordinates/figures of whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive-function domain) and an auditory target detection task. It reports group-level, voxelwise task activation maps (group t-maps and thresholded activation networks), and within-group contrasts (sustained attention > fixation; average 1–2–3 back > ‘look for X’). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are presented (figures/tables of activations and ROIs) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Participants are human (healthy adults). The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function in ASD and controls. It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (Random > Baseline; Stimulus-Oriented > Stimulus-Independent) analyzed with SPM2 across whole-brain volumes, includes coordinate tables and corrected thresholds, and describes results for each group separately. Tasks map onto executive domains (random generation: inhibition/cognitive flexibility; alphabet task: attentional selection/multitasking/prospective memory). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract confirms a PET task (degraded CPT) examining glucose metabolism correlated with task performance, so I5 (PET task) and I6 (vigilance/executive domain) are met, and I9 (participant groups) is met. However, the available content does not allow verification of I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) or I8 (at least one within-group task contrast such as task vs baseline). The abstract reports region correlations for selected regions, which could reflect ROI-only analyses (potential E3), but this cannot be confirmed. Because core article content (methods, voxelwise results, statistical maps) is missing, inclusion criteria I7 and I8 cannot be confirmed; therefore the study is excluded pending full text. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be definitively applied from the abstract alone.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm of vigilance/selective attention (executive domain: vigilance). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses and provides group-level within-group contrasts (S vs NS, time-on-task covariate) with coordinates and thresholded statistical maps. Participants are a healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion met: E3 — the study reports region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (template-based rMRGlc and discriminant/factor analyses) and does not present voxelwise, whole‑brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. (b) Inclusion met: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory, an executive function domain), I8 (within-group contrasts reported: DMS vs IMS and task vs rest within JME and control groups), I9 (clinical participant group included). (c) Inclusion not met: I7 — no voxelwise whole-brain analysis or voxelwise statistical maps are reported, so the study does not satisfy the requirement for voxelwise whole-brain evidence. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it only provides ROI-based results and lacks the voxelwise activation maps required by the review criteria.

Only the title, metadata, and abstract are provided (fulltext_incomplete=true). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm all required inclusion criteria are met. No exclusion criteria E3–E6 are met on the available information. Recommend obtaining the full text to confirm whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses before inclusion.

This is an event-related fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM99) and within-group contrasts (rating vs baseline; remembered vs forgotten). Although the authors interpret some PFC activity in terms of working memory/semantic processes, the paradigm does not operationalize a canonical executive function task. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). This is an event-related fMRI study using an antisaccade/active-fixation paradigm that directly probes inhibition (an executive function). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (including voxelwise thresholding with Bonferroni correction) and presents within-group task contrasts (inhibition vs prosaccade; individual inhibition t maps for controls and patients). Whole-brain coordinates are reported for significant clusters (striatum). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with voxelwise, within-group contrasts are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that manipulated working memory load parametrically during a grammaticality judgment task. Working memory is an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (fixed-effect group maps, cluster thresholds) and within-group contrasts (linear effects of distance, direct contrasts between conditions). Participants were healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results and coordinates are reported in text/tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded per E4: this paper reports only connectivity analyses (coherence) and coherence-difference maps (seed-based functional connectivity) rather than task-evoked voxelwise activation maps. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI study assessing executive function — spatial working memory) and I6 (task falls within working memory domain), and I9 (healthy participant within-group data). Inclusion not met: I7 (no task-evoked whole-brain voxelwise activation map reported in this paper) and I8 (no within-group voxelwise task activation contrast reported for BOLD activation; the within-group contrasts are of connectivity/coherence, not task-evoked activation). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Abstract and metadata indicate an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (participants maintained object locations), meeting executive-function domain requirements. The abstract describes voxelwise analyses of individual voxels and group-level activation modulated by task demands (suggesting whole-brain, voxelwise group results) and within-group contrasts across task difficulty (e.g., one vs three objects; 2D vs 3D), supporting inclusion. There is no indication the study reports only ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or is non-empirical. However, only title/abstract/metadata are provided here (full text not supplied), so fulltext_incomplete is flagged; I recommend obtaining the complete article to confirm specifics (e.g., explicit statement of group-level voxelwise statistical maps and reporting of coordinates/figures).

This is an fMRI task-based study explicitly probing an executive function (attention switching within verbal working memory). It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests for task activation and a repeated-measures voxelwise ANOVA across switching frequency) with whole-brain slice coverage. Within-group contrasts are presented (task vs rest and parametric modulation of switching frequency), and results are reported in tables and figures with coordinates. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present in the provided text.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using a number-size congruity (numerical Stroop) task that targets interference/inhibition (executive control). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM99 analyses (random-effects) with within-group contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent, distance effects) and provides whole-brain activation tables and coordinates. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (an executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level task activation maps (NT vs CT) derived from individual within-subject contrasts and a group t-map with whole-brain correction (Bonferroni), indicating whole-brain, voxelwise analyses. Tasks (Sternberg WM task, dual-task) clearly fall within executive function domains. Within-group task contrasts are reported/used (individual NT/PT maps and NT versus CT group map), and results are described in the text/tables/figures. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included.

This study reports task-based fMRI (N-Back working memory) assessing an executive function domain (working memory). It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (2-Back > 0-Back), with within-group task contrasts and reporting of activation results (figures and SI tables). Participants are healthy humans; behavioral and imaging results are described at the group level and voxelwise (SPM2), with coordinates and cluster reports. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria (it is empirical, reports voxelwise task activations, and includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary materials referenced).

This study reports an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control using a modified emotional Stroop paradigm (an inhibition/executive-control domain). It provides group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and reports whole-brain voxelwise one-sample t-tests with cluster thresholds and regional results in tables/figures. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and control groups; at least one within-group task contrast is reported for each group. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive processes using a go/no-go paradigm (inhibition and conflict), meeting the meta-analysis scope. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM contrasts such as “incompatible vs. neutral”, “effect tones vs. neutral”) with coordinates and figures/tables. Within-group task contrasts are presented for healthy participants. Results are reported in text, tables, and figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level within-group contrasts and discusses DLPFC activation related to conflict, the task is a perceptual judgment about synesthetic color (button press whether a letter induces synesthesia) rather than an established executive-function paradigm (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (task not within established executive function domains). I5 partially satisfied insofar as the modality is fMRI, but because I5 requires assessment of executive function/cognitive control via task-based paradigm, this is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise GLM analyses at the group level separating maintenance and selection contrasts, with whole-brain activation maps and coordinates (tables/figures). Within-group task contrasts (memory maintenance vs control, selection vs baseline) are reported. Participants are healthy human adults. The report includes whole-brain voxelwise results (figures and tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of task activations in executive function.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a two-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). Methods report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and provide within-group task contrasts (WM minus 0-back reference) and bi-directional cognitive subtractions; results are reported as group activation maps and tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function (I5), uses a working memory task (I6), reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (I7), includes within-group task contrasts (I8), participant group is acceptable (I9), and reports voxelwise results/coordinates in text/tables/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Available content is limited to title, metadata, and abstract; the study clearly reports task-based fMRI of working memory (satisfies I5 and I6). However the full text is not provided, so I cannot verify critical inclusion criteria: (I7) whether a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported, and (I8) whether a within-group task contrast is reported and presented as voxelwise results. Because those inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete record, the study is excluded pending full-text verification. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata only. While the study is a PET task-based investigation of working memory in schizophrenia (meeting I5, I6), and reports within-group task vs fixation contrasts in participants (meeting I8 and I9), the full article (methods/results) is not available here to confirm that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis/map was reported (I7). I cannot verify whether results are reported as voxelwise, whole-brain statistical maps or only as ROI/summary descriptions. Because I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the available abstract.

This study reports task-based fMRI using an executive function task (N-back working memory), collected whole-brain on 3T and analyzed voxelwise with SPM99. Single-subject within-task contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) were generated and used in group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper reports group-level task-evoked activation effects (including coordinates in MNI space) and genotype-based group comparisons of the task contrast; the methods explicitly describe voxelwise processing and reported loci for task-related activation. Although some significance was reported with correction within a PFC ROI, the study conducted and reported voxelwise, group-level task contrasts and provides coordinates/figures. Participants include healthy controls (and clinical samples elsewhere in paper), satisfying participant criteria. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (inhibition/selective attention) in OCD patients and controls, with whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses reported (SPM, voxelwise thresholds and cluster reporting). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (task vs control) and pre-post within-patient contrasts following behavioral therapy, and provides coordinates/tables/figures of whole-brain results. The Stroop task falls within established executive function domains (inhibition). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating cognitive control/executive processes (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring) using letter and visuospatial decision tasks. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation results (coordinates and statistical maps described) including within-group contrasts (letter vs visuospatial; tasks vs baseline). Participants are healthy right-handed volunteers (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as voxelwise activations with coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (syllable WM), reporting group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects), whole-brain acquisition/analysis with coordinates and activation maps, and within-group contrasts (task vs rest and paired task comparisons). Participants are healthy native Japanese adults. Results are reported in figures/tables (coordinates). All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes within-group, voxelwise contrasts relevant to executive function (working memory). The authors report group-level SPM analyses (contrasts: game>dot, game>scene, game>random) with whole-brain voxelwise results corrected for multiple comparisons and tables of activation foci. The task explicitly includes a working-memory component (game>dot) which maps to the review’s executive function domain. Whole-brain imaging and voxelwise group contrasts are reported, and results are presented in text/tables. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using verbal and non-verbal working memory tasks (an executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise working-memory minus baseline contrasts, group-level whole-brain activation maps and voxelwise regression analyses linking PCS scores to BOLD changes. Analyses were normalized to MNI space and thresholded voxelwise; results are presented as group activation maps and VOI/voxelwise findings. Participants (concussed athlete subgroups and controls) are acceptable per the review. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full article content (background, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (delayed cued recall), which falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (including contrasts of maintenance vs control and lexicality effects), with coordinates and thresholded maps described and supplemental data available. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., maintenance vs case-judgment control; words vs pseudowords; load effects). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive working memory (dual-task WM span). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM random-effects and conjunctions) with tables of peak coordinates and corrected statistics, and within-group task contrasts (Read+Remember vs Read, Read+Remember vs Remember). Tasks clearly fall within the executive function domain (working memory/dual-task coordination). Although Experiment 1 used limited slice coverage, analyses were voxelwise and group-level; Experiment 2 used whole-brain acquisition. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting) using modified WCST paradigms. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99, FDR-corrected maps) and within-group task contrasts (A minus D and decomposed contrasts A–B, B–C, C–D). Participant group (n=21 healthy adults) is reported. Results are presented in text, figures, and tables with coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete.

This fMRI study includes a Stroop task (inhibition), an established executive function domain, and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (ICA and voxelwise comparisons) with tables/figures of whole-brain results. Within-group task contrasts are presented (Stroop task blocks vs rest; moral dilemma vs control). Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full-text is complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Empirical event-related fMRI study using task-based paradigms including a Stroop task (inhibition/conflict) and a time-estimation performance-monitoring task, meeting executive-function domain criteria. Voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses are reported (contrasts: correct vs error feedback; incongruent vs congruent; errors vs correct) with coordinates/regions described (Table 1, figures), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting even though slice coverage was limited. At least one within-group task contrast is reported for healthy participants. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an empirical neuroimaging report). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Included for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory with distraction (executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM2; random-effects, corrected for multiple comparisons) and presents within-group task contrasts (main effects of cue, delay, distraction, selection) for adults and children, with tables/figures of activations. Participant groups include developmental samples (children and adults). Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

Although this is an fMRI, task-based study of attention-to-prepulse (an attention/vigilance task) in unmedicated schizophrenia-spectrum and control participants and includes voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (inclusion I5, I6, I7, I9, I10 are satisfied), the paper’s whole-brain results and SPM reporting focus on between-group attend-minus-ignore contrasts. The full text does not present or report any group-level within-group task activation maps/contrasts (e.g., task vs. baseline or attend vs. baseline) for any single group. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast). Inclusion criterion I8 (at least one within-group task contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete. Hence excluded.

The full text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study that assesses intrinsic alertness / vigilance (an executive-domain: vigilance) using within-subject task contrasts. Group-level, voxelwise SPM99 analyses (random-effects second-level) are reported with voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures of whole-brain activation coordinates, including contrasts of each task vs rest and a distributed-vs-focused within-group subtraction. The methods, results, and discussion are present (full text complete). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function (vigilance) fMRI with within-group voxelwise whole-brain results.

Full text appears incomplete (only metadata and header present). No information in the provided content indicates a task-based PET study of executive function. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no evidence the PET study assessed executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no tasks within executive domains described), I7 (no report of whole-brain voxelwise group-level task maps), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I10 (no whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none explicitly by available content. Because the full article text (methods, results) is not provided, I cannot determine whether the study contains qualifying activation contrasts; fulltext_incomplete=true for downstream review.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (SPM2) with within-group task contrasts (e.g. Space>NonSpace, AlloSpace–EgoSpace, AlloSpace–Baseline), provides MNI coordinates and figures, and reports behavioral–activation correlations. The sample is a healthy adult within-group cohort. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg task), an executive function domain. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; whole-brain corrected thresholds) and provides within-group task contrasts (average encoding, maintenance, retrieval vs baseline; parametric load regressions). Results are presented as statistical maps, tables of peak coordinates, and figures. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a GO–NOGO paradigm examining action planning/inhibition effects on visual encoding. The GO–NOGO task is an established inhibition (executive function) domain; analyses include within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (NOGO vs GO; GO vs nonevents) using random-effects one-sample t-tests, reported with coordinates and figures. Experiment 1 reports whole-brain coverage; Experiment 2 has partial-brain coverage (occipito-temporal), but voxelwise analyses are reported, which meets the allowance for partial coverage. Results are reported in tables/figures and fully include introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function with within-group voxelwise contrasts and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly investigates planning and online control of action sequences — processes that map onto established executive function domains (planning and working memory). The study used a task-based paradigm with healthy adult participants, provides within-group voxelwise analyses (voxel-wise one-way ANOVAs on AUC estimates; reported whole-brain ROIs and coordinate tables), and reports within-group contrasts (IG vs. EG, complexity effects, premovement vs movement). Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps/ROIs and detailed tables/figures of coordinates. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm (PASAT) that probes executive functions, primarily working memory and attention. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain statistical maps and corrected p-values, includes Talairach coordinates and tables of activation sites, and presents multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., PASAT vs rest; repeat prior vs repeat immediate). Participants are a healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) are present, so full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of mental arithmetic designed to induce working memory load (an executive function domain). It includes voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (one-sample t-tests and F-/t- maps) contrasting mental arithmetic vs reference baseline (within-group task contrast), with whole-brain preprocessing and thresholding (FDR/FWE) and coordinates/figures/tables of activations. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the delayed recognition portion of the Word Memory Test, which is a working memory/episodic retrieval task. The paper reports a within-group, voxelwise group-level contrast (test vs control) analyzed with SPM2 and displays whole-brain results (FWE-corrected maps, table and figure of activations). Participants are healthy adults; participant group eligibility is acceptable. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, so full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that manipulates calculation complexity to engage working memory/executive processes (complex vs simple arithmetic). It reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain contrasts (complex > simple) for each operator with Talairach/MNI coordinates and FDR correction, and a conjunction analysis. The design uses within-group task contrasts (complex vs simple) in an adult sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures described) is provided. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function-related (working memory) task activations and provides whole-brain, within-group voxelwise results suitable for inclusion.

This full-text PET study reports task-based executive-function (working memory) activations using group-level voxelwise analyses. It meets inclusion criteria: I5 (PET task-based study of executive function), I6 (working memory tasks), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and an exploratory search of grey matter with corrected thresholds), I8 (within-group contrasts reported: spatial span vs visuomotor control, spatial manipulation vs control, and manipulation vs span), I9 (within-group results from healthy adult participants), and I10 (results reported as stereotaxic coordinates in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical study). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Hence include in meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based spatial working memory paradigm (executive function). The paper reports within-group task-versus-baseline contrasts, derives group-level voxelwise t-maps (signal-change maps transformed to Talairach and group composite t-maps), and presents whole-brain/timecourse results. Participant groups include clinical (schizophrenia) and healthy controls. Reporting includes figures and text describing activation peaks and HRF-convolved analyses. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation mapping and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The supplied full text appears incomplete (title, abstract, and metadata only). Abstract confirms this is a task-based fMRI Stroop study involving synaesthetes (so I5 and I6 are satisfied) and includes synaesthete and control participant groups (I9 satisfied). However, the available content does not provide methods or results needed to confirm: whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps (I7); presence of at least one within-group task contrast (I8); or that whole-brain results are reported in an acceptable form (I10). Because I7–I8 (and I10) cannot be verified from the incomplete text, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be confidently applied from the abstract alone, so none are listed.

This is a task-based PET study of working memory (an established executive function) using within-subject, within-group contrasts. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed with SPM99 and group-level contrasts/conjunctions reported with coordinates. Tasks (WM, semantic control, baseline) clearly probe working memory load and retrieval type; contrasts (e.g., WM vs BL, sign vs speech) are voxelwise and reported at the group level. Participants form a defined group (early bilingual interpreters) and the paper reports empirical neuroimaging activation maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of attentional control (a Stroop-like inhibition/conflict task), reporting within-subject interference-vs-control voxelwise group analyses and behavioral correlates. The paper presents whole-brain voxelwise group random-effects analyses, tables and figures with coordinates, and within-group contrasts across cycles. Partial brain coverage (15 slices) is acceptable per criteria because analyses are voxelwise and reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task, imaging modality, whole-brain voxelwise group contrast, within-group contrasts, and reporting of results.

Although this is an fMRI study of decision-making that probes cognitive-control/conflict processes and reports within-group contrasts, the primary group-level analyses were restricted to a priori anatomical ROIs and results are reported as small-volume-corrected peaks (3 mm spheres). The paper does not present a whole‑brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map (analysis was confined to ROI volumes), so it fails the requirement for whole‑brain voxelwise evidence. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI / small-volume-corrected analyses). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI), I6 (task taps cognitive control/conflict), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (developmental participant groups allowed). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole‑brain voxelwise group-level task activation map reported). Full text appears complete.

Full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported: Magic > Causal Control, Surprise > Causal Control, etc.), I9 (healthy adult participant group; within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and described in text). Did NOT meet I6: the experimental task (passive viewing of magic trick videos with attention checks) does not clearly fall within the specified established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors interpret activations in terms of cognitive control/conflict monitoring (relating to ACC and DLPFC), the primary paradigm is perceptual belief-violation and not a canonical EF task; therefore it fails I6. I5 is borderline: while the paper discusses cognitive control processes, the task was not designed as an established executive-function task. Because I6 is not satisfied, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) were triggered.

This is a task-based PET study using the Iowa Gambling Task (an executive decision-making/planning task) with voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported. The paper reports within-subject task contrasts (active minus control), performs group-level random-effects analyses, and also reports a within-group (fixed-effects) analysis in controls with peak coordinates and cluster statistics. Whole-brain normalized rCBF results and coordinates are reported across prefrontal and other regions. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study with task-based contrasts that probe cognitive control demands (listening, selective attention, working memory and response selection when repeating the last word in sentences under varying noise levels). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (e.g., Speech vs Quiet, SPIN vs Quiet, SPIN vs Speech) with coordinates/clusters and discusses activation in frontal, cingulate, cerebellar and temporal regions. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a go–nogo paradigm (response inhibition/cognitive control). It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects, voxelwise Z-thresholding and cluster correction) and contrasts including go vs nogo and compatibility interactions. Results are presented as brain activation tables/figures and described in the text. Participants were a healthy adult sample (N=12). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of executive function (inhibition), whole-brain voxelwise results, within-group task contrasts, and reporting of coordinates/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attentional control/Stroop (inhibition) that reports group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts. The paper reports within-group contrasts (incongruent vs. neutral; incongruent-eligible vs. incongruent-ineligible), voxelwise repeated-measures ANOVA and blocked analyses with Z-score maps and Talairach coordinates, and whole-brain (albeit limited-slice) coverage. Results are reported as activation maps and coordinate tables. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a sustained attention (vigilance) task, which falls within established executive function domains. The full text reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects, voxel-by-voxel ANOVA) and provides within-group task contrasts (novel and practice blocks versus fixation/baseline) for both cocaine and control groups. Results are described in detail (methods, results, tables/figures referenced) and thus meet the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a working-memory task (Exp.1) and an attention task (Exp.2), both task-based manipulations of executive/cognitive-control domains (working memory and sustained attention). The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (ANOVAs), with within-group task contrasts (e.g. high vs low memory load; high vs low attentional load) and task-evoked activation maps presented in figures/tables. Participant sample and results are reported in full (methods, image acquisition, GLM and group analyses, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical content). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (spatial n-back), meeting executive function domain requirements. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) analyzed with SPM and reports significant activation clusters (right inferior frontal gyrus, right intraparietal sulcus) with corrected p-values and cluster sizes, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise evidence. A within-group task contrast is explicitly presented for the healthy subject group. Full article sections (methods, results, discussion) are provided, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using n-back working memory paradigms (verbal and spatial) in 31 healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects, cluster-thresholded Z-statistic maps) including within-group contrasts (2-back > 0-back; verbal > spatial). Results are presented in figures, tables, and text with peak coordinates. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (fMRI task of executive function/working memory; tasks within executive domains; whole-brain voxelwise group analysis; within-group task contrasts; participant group reported; whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, the study is an empirical fMRI investigation of visual working memory, so I5 (fMRI task-based) and I6 (working memory, an executive domain) are satisfied. However, the abstract does not provide sufficient detail to verify I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps), I8 (at least one within-group task contrast reported), or I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the available text. Because core methods/results required to confirm all inclusion criteria are missing and fulltext_incomplete=true, the study cannot be included at this stage.

This is an event-related fMRI, task-based empirical study of reversal learning (a form of cognitive flexibility/set switching), reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., CR>BL, FRE>BL, FRE>PENS+PRE) using SPM2 with results presented in tables and figures. Participants are a within-group healthy volunteer sample. All required within-group voxelwise contrasts are reported and results are available in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Simon task (inhibition/cognitive control) in older adult participants. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (incongruent > congruent contrast) with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and tables of coordinates and figures. Methods, results, and discussion are provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task domain, imaging modality, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visuo-spatial working memory (working memory = established executive function domain).
